narrative.overview:
The Portfolio's Visual language is a dark, confident engineering page where bold, tightly tracked type and hairline panels carry the authority and the facts lead. The Owner stays in the background: a small, plain photo beside the name, never a portrait as the centrepiece.

The system is monochrome bone and ink. Dark is the default, always: a near-black ground carries warm bone ink. The complete light theme puts the same ink on bone paper and appears only when the visitor picks it in the dark and light switch, never from the system preference. Every colour token resolves both themes through `light-dark()`, so the active colour scheme picks one. Secondary text, metadata, hairlines and tints are the ink itself at fixed alpha steps; there is no hued accent anywhere. The primary action is the ink, filled; focus is an ink ring. The only hue in the system is error.

About me has its own, entirely distinct Visual language. It restyles the shared navigation, language toggle and Footer through tokens alone; their place and behavior never change.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default, always; light a complete equal the visitor switches to; both WCAG 2.2 AA.
Monochrome: bone ink on near-black, ink on bone paper, secondary ink and hairlines by alpha steps of the ink.
No hued accent: the primary action is filled ink, every other button is outlined in a hairline, row links are unboxed text, focus is an ink ring.
Bold display grotesk with tight tracking; monospace only for labels, tags, chips and numerals.
Hairline-bordered panel grids whose cells share borders, instead of cards and shadows.
Facts over the person: a hairline facts panel leads Home, the photo stays small.

rules.name: The Ink Is The Action Rule
rules.body: There is no accent colour. The primary action is the ink filled, with the ground as its text: one per view. Secondary buttons are outlined in Hairline Control; row links stay unboxed. Focus is an ink ring. If a view needs colour to show what to do next, the hierarchy is wrong, not the palette.

rules.name: The Alpha Steps Rule
rules.body: Secondary, muted, hairline and tint colours are always the ink mixed toward transparent at their fixed steps (84, 64, 26, 22, 10, 7, 4), and the Wash is the ink at 2% mixed into the ground; never new greys. The exceptions are few and named: input borders, set per theme to hold 3:1 (52% ink on paper, 44% bone on night); the raised surfaces (Night Raised, Paper Raised); and the float shadow, whose ring and shadow are the ink at 6% and 22% on paper and bone at 30% over black at 60% on night, because no ink is darker than the night ground.

rules.name: The Only Hue Is Error Rule
rules.body: Error is the sole hued colour, and it appears only where something went wrong.

rules.name: The Two Equal Themes Rule
rules.body: Every colour token exists in both themes and passes AA in both; dark is designed first, never light inverted.

rules.name: The Mono Labels Rule
rules.body: Monospace sets labels, tags, chips and numerals, never sentences or headings, and never as an eyebrow above a heading: the heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Hairline Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Reach for a hairline or a tint step first; a shadow is the last resort and only for something floating above the page.

dos: Do design the dark theme first and keep the light theme a complete equal, both at WCAG 2.2 AA.
Do open every Page in dark; show light only after the visitor picks it in the switch.
Do make the one primary action per view filled ink, and outline every other button in a hairline.
Do derive every secondary, muted, hairline and tint colour from the ink at its fixed alpha step.
Do lead Home with the facts in a hairline panel (role, seniority, location, work model, technologies) and keep the Owner's photo small and plain beside the name.
Do take every visual value from tokens, so About me can restyle the shared navigation, language toggle and Footer through tokens alone.
Do give every component all its states (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, and loading, error or success where they apply) before it counts as done.
Do keep motion to short expo ease-out transitions (150ms for controls, 200ms for panels, 240ms for the theme crossfade), no bounce, and 0ms under reduced motion.
donts: Don't introduce a hued accent, a gradient or a multi-colour palette; the Owner turned down every one offered.
Don't use error red for anything but errors.
Don't follow the system colour scheme preference; the Owner chose dark always by default.
Don't build a template portfolio: no avatar hero, no skill pills, no grid of identical project cards.
Don't set a monospace eyebrow above a heading, or monospace prose.
Don't make the Owner's photo a centrepiece: no large portrait, no colour effects, no full-bleed photo.
Don't put a shadow on anything that doesn't float above the page.
Don't let expression cost the 30-second read: role, seniority, technologies, location, CV and contact stay findable at a glance.

aboutMe.overview:
About me's Visual language sets the Owner's interests, recommendations and studies like a gig poster: flat colour bands, one per Section, a condensed uppercase display that runs the band's width, and lists set as a poster's billing. It is loud and warm where the Portfolio is quiet, and it never looks like a social profile, a gamer costume, the Portfolio recoloured, or anything corporate or cold.

It loads over the Portfolio's tokens and redefines the same names, so the shared components take most of its look through tokens; the differences that have no token yet are listed under Components. Spacing and motion stay the Portfolio's. It has one theme and no photo. Each band sets every colour token itself, so a component inside a band takes that band's colours. Illustration is optional: the language works without it, and the first band reserves a slot for one.
keyCharacteristics: Four flat bands, purple, sunset orange, lime and charcoal, rotating one per Section.
One theme and no theme switch; no photo; the language toggle keeps its place.
Big Shoulders Display, condensed and uppercase, sized to the band's width; Archivo for everything else.
Lists as poster billing: the category in large display type in the band's two key colours, the item in heavy uppercase Archivo in the band's ink.
One ink per band at full strength, no alpha steps; 3px ink rules and square corners.
No shadows, no blur, no gradients, no neon; an error is a dashed ink rule and its message, never a hue.

rules.name: The One Band Per Section Rule
rules.body: Every Section owns one band, and the bands rotate purple, sunset, lime, charcoal. A component never sets a palette colour; it reads the tokens of the band it sits in.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Each band has one ink at full strength: secondary, muted, hairline, control and input colours are the ink itself, and tints are transparent. On sunset any alpha step below full ink drops under 4.5:1. Three lines take another colour: the lineup's block rules are in Key; a hovered edge (`--color-hairline-hover`) is the Display colour; and hover and focus underlines on the language toggle, band links and lineup items are 3px in Key or Key Alt.

rules.name: The Cream Is Large Rule
rules.body: Cream holds only 3.3:1 on sunset, so on the sunset ground it sets large type only: display, headlines and the billing keys. On the charcoal action fill it is the action's text, at 15:1.

rules.name: The No Error Hue Rule
rules.body: No single hue reads on all four bands, so error is the band's ink, drawn as a dashed rule with its message, never a colour alone.

rules.name: The Band-Wide Title Rule
rules.body: The Page title is sized from its container's width (24cqi, from 3.5rem to 20rem), so it runs the band's width like a poster's lettering.

rules.name: The Billing Rule
rules.body: A list is a lineup: the category in the display face at title size, large type, in the band's two key colours, alternating Key and Key Alt down the list; the item in heavy uppercase Archivo at billing size in the band's ink; two 3px rules in Key above and below. On sunset the keys are charcoal and cream, so half the categories share the ink and stand apart by face and size.

rules.name: The Printed Flat Rule
rules.body: Nothing on About me casts or blurs; separate with a 3px ink rule or a change of band.

dos: Do give every Section one band, rotating purple, sunset, lime and charcoal, with the bar and intro on purple and the Footer on the next band in the rotation.
Do let a component read its band's tokens; never set a palette colour on a component.
Do set text in the band's one ink at full strength, and cream only at large sizes on sunset.
Do size the Page title from its container so it runs the band's width, in Big Shoulders Display, uppercase.
Do set lists as billing: the category in large display type in the band's two key colours, the item in heavy uppercase Archivo, underlined in its category colour on hover and focus.
Do mark an error with a dashed 3px ink rule and its message.
Do keep the language toggle in its place and leave the theme switch out.
Do make every band work without an illustration; the slot is optional.
donts: Don't add a shadow, a blur, a gradient or neon; the bands are flat and printed.
Don't step the ink down by alpha; on sunset every step below full ink falls under 4.5:1.
Don't give error a hue; no single hue reads on all four bands.
Don't let it look like a social profile (cards, counters, feeds), a gamer or childish costume, the Portfolio recoloured, or anything corporate or cold.
Don't use Dance Gavin Dance's artwork, lettering or logo; the poster grammar is an own version.
Don't add a photo or a second theme.
Don't round a corner unless the thing is truly round.
